newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik government troops advance on rebel commander.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government troops advance on rebel commander.

text.p: Troops loyal to Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov advanced on Monday on the rebel-held town of Kabodien in southern Tajikistan, one of two strongholds of mutinous Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev.
A Reuters correspondent on the spot said the troops, armed with more than 60 units of artillery and equipment, had stopped about 10 km (six miles) from the town.
The correspondent said it was not yet clear when they planned to try to capture Kabodien, 160 km (100 miles) southwest of the capital Dushanbe.
The new standoff follows more than a week of turmoil in Tajikistan, sparked by a struggle between competing warlords and presidential forces.

It came just weeks after Rakhmonov, who is backed by Moscow, signed a peace agreement with Islamic opposition guerrillas aimed at ending four years of civil war in the impoverished former Soviet republic bordering on Afghanistan.

The Islamic guerrillas were not involved in the latest clashes, which erupted on August 9 when fighting broke out between rival warlords in the capital Dushanbe and Khodoyberdyev moved his brigade towards the city.
Russia, which has around 20,000 troops in Tajikistan dominating a Commonwealth of Independent States peacekeeping force, has kept a low profile in the latest crisis.

But Russian peacekeepers have brokered peace talks, hoping to stabilise the country of 5.7 millions, which Moscow sees as a buffer against the spread of Islamic fundamentalism, but which is riven by internal rivalries.
Khudoberdyev began pulling his troops back on Wednesday after losing a strategic aluminium-producing town west of Dushanbe to presidential forces.
But one of his allies said on Saturday they had simply regrouped further south. "We will fight to the bitter end," Lieutenant-Colonel Sergei Zavarygin told Reuters.

On their way to Kabodien, the presidential troops encountered fierce resistance around a bridge near the village of Garavuti. This straddles routes to the Shaartuz and Kabodien regions where the rebels' main forces are concentrated.
The head of a presidential special brigade told Reuters one soldier on his side had been killed in fighting and 11 wounded. There was no word on the casualties on the other side.
Itar-Tass news agency earlier quoted government military officials as saying 50 rebels were killed during the operation while three government soldiers died and about 10 were wounded.
Shaartuz is further south along the Aktau mountain range. Kabodien is an obstacle on the way to Shaartuz, close to the border with Uzbekistan to the west and Afghanistan to the south.

Interfax news agency earlier quoted the head of the Presidential Guard, General Gafar Mirzoyev, as saying government troops had encircled Khudoyberdyev's units, which numbered about 1,400 men, three tanks and several armoured personnel carriers.

"They may be driven to the Tajik-Uzbek border or they may be driven to the Tajik-Afghan border. But it will be practically impossible for them to cross the border. The only option for Khudoyberdyev is to lay down his arms," Mirzoyev said.
Mirzoyev also said that Khudoyberdyev's men were using Grad multiple missile launchers and artillery against his troops. There was no independent confirmation of the report.
